p1.original: 8.1 大脑同时在意识和无意识的多个水平上运作。
p1.en: 8.1 The brain operates simultaneously at multiple levels of consciousness and unconsciousness.

p2.original: 8.2 意识的周期性波动与我们的生物节律和环境中的刺激模式相对应。
p2.en: 8.2 The cyclical fluctuations of awareness correspond to the stimuli in our biological rhythms and environment.

p3.original: 8.3 当通过心理、行为或化学方法改变正常意识的某些方面时，意识状态就会改变。
p3.en: 8.3 When certain aspects of normal consciousness are changed through psychological, behavioural or chemical methods, the state of consciousness changes.

p4.original: 你是否做过这样一个梦，你如此享受它以至于不想起床，这样就可以继续你的美梦？在凤凰城六月的一个炎热的早晨，一位家庭主妇、三个孩子的母亲刚从这样的梦中醒来（Meyer，2011）。
p4.en: Have you ever had a dream that you enjoy so much that you don't want to get up so that you can continue your dream? In June, a hot morning in Phoenix, a housewife, the mother of three children, just woke up from such a dream (Meyer, 2011).

p5.original: 在我的梦中，有一对情侣正在树林里的草地上进行着紧张的谈话。这两个人中一个人就是普通女孩，而另一人则英俊极了，光彩照人，是一个吸血鬼。他们正在讨论现实情况中的困境：他们彼此相爱，然而女孩血液的香味异乎寻常地吸引着吸血鬼，他难以克制自己立即杀死女孩的冲动。
p5.en: In my dream, a couple was having a nervous conversation on the grass in the woods. One of these two is an ordinary girl, while the other one is handsome, glamorous, and a vampire. They are discussing the dilemmas of the reality: they love each other, yet the scent of the girl's blood attracts vampires in an extraordinary way, and he has no control over the urge to kill the girl immediately.

p6.original: 这位家庭主妇被梦中极其英俊的男青年迷住了，并且也被这对情侣的个性和所面临的困境所打动，于是，她开始创作一个有关他们的故事——这个故事很快被创作为名为《暮光之城》（Twilight）的系列畅销书和电影。
p6.en: The housewife was fascinated by the very handsome young man in her dreams and was also impressed by the personal nature and difficulties faced by the couple, and she began to write a story about them — a story that was quickly written as a series of best-selling books and films called Twilight.

p7.original: 斯蒂芬妮·梅尔（Stephenie Meyer）并不是第一个受到梦境启发的人。自古以来，梦就被视为洞察力、创造力和预言的源泉。例如，我们可以在《旧约》（Old Testament）希伯来人约瑟（Joseph）的故事中看到这一点，他将法老梦见肥牛和瘦牛解释为埃及将会在经历了丰收之年后，进入饥荒之年（Genesis 41:1-7）。
p7.en: Stephanie Meyer was not the first person inspired by a dream. Since ancient times, dreams have been seen as a source of insight, creativity and prophecy. For example, we can see this in the story of the old Testament, the Hebrew Joseph, who explained that Pharaoh's dream of fat and thin cattle was that Egypt would enter the year of famine after the harvest (Genesis 41:1-7).

p8.original: 英国诗人塞缪尔·泰勒·柯勒律治（Samuel Taylor Coleridge）将他的诗歌《忽必烈汗》（Kubla Khan）中的意象归功于他在阅读了那位著名的蒙古战士的传记后所做的一个梦（可能是由药物引起的）。同样，超现实主义艺术家萨尔瓦多·达利（Salvador Dali）发现，梦是生动意象的源泉。莫扎特、贝多芬、披头士乐队和斯汀（Sting）等多位作曲家都将某些作品归功于他们在梦境中获得的灵感。在科学界，化学家奥古斯特·凯库勒（August Kekule）发现了苯分子的结构，这源于他梦见一条蛇卷成一个圈，把自己的尾巴咬在口中。甚至著名的恐怖小说作家斯蒂芬·金（Stephen King）也声称，他从自己童年的噩梦中获得了故事灵感。
p8.en: Samuel Taylor Colleridge, the British poet, attributed the image in his poem Kubla Khan to a dream he had made after reading the biography of the famous Mongolian soldier (probably drug-induced). Similarly, the super-realist artist Salvador Dali found that dreams were the source of vivid images. Several composers, such as Mozart, Beethoven, Beatles and Sting, have all attributed some of their work to the inspiration they received in their dreams. In the scientific community, August Kekule, the chemist, discovered the structure of the benzene molecule, which stemmed from his dream of having a snake roll in a circle and biting his tail in the mouth. Even Stephen King, a famous horror novelist, claimed that he had gained story inspiration from his childhood nightmare.

p10.original: 梦会帮助我们解决问题吗？
p10.en: Do dreams help us solve problems?

p11.original: 梦是否反映了我们无意识的心理活动？
p11.en: Does the dream reflect our unconscious psychological activity?

p12.original: 或者梦只是随机的心理“垃圾”——也许是前一天遗留下的各种感受的碎片？
p12.en: Or is the dream just random psycho-gamish -- maybe a fragment of the feelings left over the previous day?

p13.original: 对梦进行科学研究的困难之处在于，这些心理状态都是个人经验，任何其他人都不能直接体验你的梦。因此，这些议题将成为我们在本章中重点关注的问题。
p13.en: The difficulty of scientific research into dreams is that these mental states are personal experiences and no one else can directly experience your dreams. Those topics will therefore be the focus of our attention in this chapter.

p14.en: This chapter considers the following topics:

p15.original: 心理学家如何客观地考察梦及其他主观心理状态？
p15.en: How can psychologists objectively examine dreams and other subjective psychological situations?

p16.original: 做梦是人脑可能存在的多个意识状态之一。其他意识状态包括我们熟悉的觉醒状态和不太熟悉的催眠、冥想，以及用化学方法（如精神药物）引发的意识状态，我们都会在本章中进行研究，但这还不是全部。在这些意识状态背后，大脑的大部分工作都发生在离线状态——意识之外（Wallace & Fisher，1999）。这包括诸如从记忆中提取信息之类的日常任务（如7乘以9等于多少），以及在大脑深部区域所发生的控制基本生理功能（如血压和体温）的基本操作。介于这两个极端之间的是，大脑的某些部位以某种方式处理我们曾经有意识的记忆和本能反应，如回忆今天吃的早餐或你最尴尬的时刻等。正如我们将会看到的那样，自从弗洛伊德提出梦可能反映了不为人知的、无意识的恐惧和欲望以来，这个由无意识的想法、感觉、欲望和表象所组成的“隐秘世界”的性质一直备受争议。在本章中，我们会像其他学者那样评估这一观点，为此，我们将从熟悉的意识状态开始，其占据了我们大部分的清醒时间。
p16.en: Dreaming is one of the many states of consciousness that may exist in the human brain. Other states of consciousness, including our familiar state of awakening and unfamiliar hypnosis, meditation, and the state of consciousness caused by chemical methods, such as psychotropic substances, are all studied in this chapter, but not all of them. Behind these consciousness states, most of the brain's work occurs offline - outside of consciousness (Wallah & Fisher, 1999). This includes routine tasks such as extracting information from memory (e.g., 7 times 9 equals what) and basic operations that control basic physiological functions (e.g., blood pressure and body temperature) that occur in deep-brain areas. In between these two extremes, certain parts of the brain deal in some way with our conscious memories and instincts, such as remembering breakfast today or your most embarrassing moments. As we will see, the nature of this “hidden world” made up of unconscious thoughts, feelings, desires and appearances has been controversial since Freud's dream might reflect unknown and unconscious fears and desires. In this chapter, we will assess this view as other scholars have done, and for that we will start with a familiar state of consciousness, which takes most of our sobering time.
